```{r, include=FALSE}
highcharter::hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
```

## Translate Highcharts options to R

For the complete walkthrough with Palmer penguins, JavaScript objects and
nested R lists, see [JavaScript API Basics](highchartsjs-api-basics.html).

Tom Bishop's legend example shows how to read the Highcharts API from R.
Start with monthly temperatures. Hover over a month to compare the cities in a table.

```{r}
library(highcharter)

hc <- highcharts_demo() |> hc_tooltip(table = TRUE)
hc
```

The JavaScript legend below places the entries in the upper right and underlines
the legend title. In R, the top-level option becomes `hc_legend()` and each nested
object becomes a named list. Keep the option names in camel case.
[Highcharts legend options](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/legend).

```js
legend: {
  layout: 'vertical', align: 'right', verticalAlign: 'top',
  title: { text: 'Cities', style: { textDecoration: 'underline' } }
}
```

```{r translate-legend}
hc |>
  hc_legend(
    layout = "vertical",
    align = "right",
    verticalAlign = "top",
    title = list(text = "Cities", style = list(textDecoration = "underline"))
  )
```

## Chart layout and type

With `hc_chart` you can define general chart options.

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_chart(
    borderColor = '#EBBA95',
    borderRadius = 10,
    borderWidth = 2,
    backgroundColor = list(
      linearGradient = c(0, 0, 500, 500),
      stops = list(
        list(0, 'rgb(255, 255, 255)'),
        list(1, 'rgb(200, 200, 255)')
      )
    )
  )
```

Now change type to column and add 3d effect.

```{r}
hc <- hc |>
  hc_chart(
    type = "column",
    options3d = list(
      enabled = TRUE,
      beta = 15,
      alpha = 15
    )
  )
hc

# back to the line!
hc <- hc_chart(hc, type = "line", options3d = list(enabled = FALSE))
```

## Title, subtitle, caption and credits

A good chart always have at least title, right? Then you can do it better adding relevant information
using a subtitle or caption, even link to the source of data:

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_title(
    text = "This is the title of the chart"
  ) |>
  hc_subtitle(
    text = "This is an intereseting subtitle to give
    context for the chart or some interesting fact"
  ) |>
  hc_caption(
    text = "This is a long text to give some
    subtle details of the data which can be relevant to the reader.
    This is usually a long text that's why I'm trying to put a
    <i>loooooong</i> text.",
    useHTML = TRUE
  ) |>
  hc_credits(
    text = "Chart created using R and highcharter",
    href = "http://jkunst.com/highcharter",
    enabled = TRUE
  )
```

## Axes, ticks and plot bands

Usually is desirable get control or modify the behavior of the axis:

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_xAxis(
    title = list(text = "Month in x Axis"),
    opposite = TRUE
  ) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    title = list(text = "Temperature on the Y axis"),
    opposite = TRUE,
    minorTickInterval = "auto",
    minorGridLineDashStyle = "LongDashDotDot",
    showFirstLabel = FALSE,
    showLastLabel = FALSE
  )
```

A good feature is `plotLines` and `plotBand` which you can use in both axis. For example:

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_xAxis(
    plotLines = list(
      list(
        label = list(text = "This is a plotLine"),
        color = "#FF0000",
        width = 2,
        value = 4,
        # the zIndex is used to put the label text over the grid lines
        zIndex = 1
      )
    )
  ) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    plotBands = list(
      list(
        from = 20,
        to = 50,
        color = hex_to_rgba("red", 0.1),
        label = list(text = "This is a plotBand"),
        # the zIndex is used to put the label text over the grid lines
        zIndex = 1
      )
    )
  )
```

## Category order

Sort the frequency table to display the most common cylinder count first.
`hchart()` keeps that order and uses the dimension name for the axis title.

```{r category-order}
counts <- sort(table(Cylinders = mtcars$cyl), decreasing = TRUE)
hchart(counts, name = "Cars")
```

For another common adjustment, see [Keep other series visible on hover](#keep-other-series-visible-on-hover).

For a layout with several pairs of axes, see [Multiple axes](multiple-axes.html).

## Legend & tooltip

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_legend(
    align = "left",
    verticalAlign = "top",
    layout = "vertical",
    x = 0,
    y = 100
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    crosshairs = TRUE,
    backgroundColor = "#F0F0F0",
    shared = TRUE,
    borderWidth = 5
  )
```

For a chart inside the tooltip, see [Charts inside tooltips](showcase.html#charts-inside-tooltips).

### HTML table legend

An external table can show summary statistics next to each series name.
`hc_legend(enabled = FALSE)` hides the built-in legend. HTML supplies the
table and buttons, CSS styles their visible state, and the click handler
calls the native `series.setVisible()` toggle.

```{r legend-table}
values <- list(North = c(3, 1, 5), South = c(2, 4, 3))
chart <- highchart() |> hc_legend(enabled = FALSE)
for (city in names(values)) {
  chart <- hc_add_series(chart, id = city, name = city, data = values[[city]])
}

tags <- htmltools::tags
toggle <- "const panel = this.closest('section');
  const chart = Highcharts.charts.find(c => c && panel.contains(c.renderTo));
  const series = chart.get(this.dataset.series);
  series.setVisible();
  this.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(series.visible));"

tags$section(
  chart,
  tags$style(".city-legend button[aria-pressed=false] { opacity: 0.55; }"),
  tags$table(
    class = "city-legend",
    tags$thead(tags$tr(lapply(c("City", "Last", "Min", "Max"), tags$th))),
    tags$tbody(lapply(names(values), function(city) {
      x <- values[[city]]
      tags$tr(
        tags$th(tags$button(
          city,
          type = "button",
          `data-series` = city,
          `aria-pressed` = "true",
          onclick = toggle
        )),
        tags$td(tail(x, 1)),
        tags$td(min(x)),
        tags$td(max(x))
      )
    }))
  )
)
```

For a legend that controls multiple widgets, see the line and pie example in
[`hc_connect()`](../reference/hc_connect.html) and [issue #183](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter/issues/183).

## Connect charts across HTML chunks

Give each chart the same group name to link its tooltip, crosshair and X zoom.
These two chunks also work in a Quarto HTML document. Drag on either chart to
zoom, then use either reset button to restore both X axes.

```{r connect-passengers}
hchart(AirPassengers) |> hc_connect("monthly")
```

```{r connect-change}
hchart(diff(AirPassengers)) |> hc_connect("monthly")
```

The first month has no corresponding change, so hovering over it clears the
second tooltip. To share a legend between a line and a pie, see the series
and point IDs in the [`hc_connect()`](../reference/hc_connect.html) example.

## Keep other series visible on hover

Move the pointer over a city to inspect it. An inactive opacity of one keeps
the other cities visible at full strength for comparison.

```{r inactive-series}
hc |> hc_plotOptions(series = list(states = list(inactive = list(opacity = 1))))
```

## Responsive layout

Resize the chart below 500 px to hide its legend. Highcharts restores the
legend when the chart grows past that width.

```{r responsive-legend}
hc |>
  hc_responsive(
    rules = list(list(
      condition = list(maxWidth = 500),
      chartOptions = list(legend = list(enabled = FALSE))
    ))
  )
```
